title: Started a bunch of small agents through Robinhood Agentic Account
author: Blotter-fyi
selftext:
I worked at Meta on applied AI for about 7 years, and am very bullish on AI for investing. Been working with Robinhood's agentic accounts for a while. Claude and ChatGPT were not letting me trade autonomously, so spun up a quick app for it.

Going to put 10k in the account this week and see if I can build some agents based on ideas. Let me know if you have any ideas/thesis I should try.

comments.author: leroylabs
comments.body:
One thesis worth testing is portfolio coordination itself. The screenshot shows Summit reserving $19.92 across 12 orders while the account has $7.93 available cash, with Seven and Sam operating as separate sleeves. What happens if another agent submits orders before Summit’s batch fills?

I’d make buying power reservation atomic across agents and log requested, approved, filled, and released amounts per sleeve. Also test a partial fill followed by a cancellation, since stranded reservations or reused cash could make the agents exceed the intended $10k allocation even when each one stays within its own budget.

replies.author: Shoddy_Peanut7320
replies.body: That's a sharp test case, and keeping reservations atomic across agents is the kind of thing that only breaks at the worst moment. I'd add a hard cap enforced outside the agents (total exposure and per-agent limits) so a stranded reservation can't push the account past the intended $10k. Logging every request, approval, fill and release with timestamps also lets you reconcile later. Timing around scheduled news matters when several agents trade at once, and Cymetica's EventTrader (event timing for earnings and macro releases) is one source for that.

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body:
I'd let each idea run on paper until it's boring before the 10k goes in. not because the agents will be dumb, but because the first failures are nearly always plumbing: a duplicate order on a retry, a position it forgot it had, a fill it assumed. cheap on paper, expensive live.

I built Quantradin as a paper account agents can trade over MCP, if you want somewhere to shake them out first. it's free, quantradin.com.
